profiles.meeting_scenario: A coordination meeting at a university-affiliated European law center preparing a joint legal briefing and supporting annexes for an EU-funded workshop on the Romanian-Ukrainian frontier. The briefing will synthesize official EU legal instruments, Romanian and Ukrainian implementing measures, and Euroregional cooperation arrangements to support a policy-facing case study titled "Europe from Exclusive Borders to Inclusive Frontiers." The agenda is to align the handoff between the lead doctrinal memo and the comparative source annexes, confirm which programme documents and institutional materials will be cited, decide what version of the source matrix will circulate to the steering group, and coordinate who maintains the shared authorities folder. The expected outcome is apparent agreement on deliverables for the next internal circulation round, without either participant realizing they are relying on slightly different assumptions about scope, source set, and readiness standards.

members.name: Elena Ionescu
members.role: Senior EU Public Law Counsel and Project Lead
members.expertise: EU external border law, cohesion policy, institutional legal analysis, policy brief drafting
members.background: Romanian-qualified lawyer who previously worked in a Brussels policy unit and now leads comparative legal workstreams at a university law center.
members.private_state: She wants a clean, board-ready internal package quickly so she can keep the workshop timeline on track and avoid reopening the framing of the paper at the steering-group level.
hidden_assumptions: When the team says 'programme documents,' it means the currently operative 2021-2027 Romania-Ukraine cooperation framework unless someone expressly says they are using archived material.
A 'source matrix' is a citation-controlled table keyed to legal instruments and provisions, not a broader thematic research chart.
If a draft is 'ready to circulate,' it only needs to be accurate enough for internal strategic review; translation polishing and source-verification can happen afterward.

The Romanian-Ukrainian 'frontier' section should stay within instruments directly governing that bilateral border space and the named Euroregions, not adjacent regional regimes unless expressly requested.

members.name: Taras Melnyk
members.expertise: Ukrainian administrative law, cross-border cooperation instruments, documentary source tracing, multilingual legal research
members.background: Ukrainian-trained legal researcher with experience compiling cross-border governance dossiers for international projects and translating institutional materials from Ukrainian and Romanian sources.
members.private_state: He wants the record to be historically and regionally complete so that the case study does not flatten the shift from neighbourhood cooperation to newer territorial cooperation arrangements.
hidden_assumptions: When people refer to the 'CBC programme documents' for this case study, they naturally include the 2014-2020 ENI Romania-Ukraine materials because those documents show the transition the paper is about.
A 'source matrix' means a working comparative chart that groups hard law, soft law, Euroregion statutes, and institutional practice by theme.
A document is not truly 'ready to circulate' if translations, quotations, and institutional names have not been verified against the original-language sources.

The 'frontier' case study reasonably includes nearby cooperation architectures that shape the border in practice, including tri-border and Black Sea-linked instruments, unless someone narrows the mandate.

misalignment_points.topic: What counts as the source matrix
misalignment_points.surface_form: Both agree that Taras will update and hand off 'the source matrix.'
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Elena means a tightly structured authorities table listing binding instruments, official documents, dates, article numbers, and citation-ready references for direct insertion into the memo package.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Taras means a broader comparative spreadsheet organizing legal instruments, soft-law texts, Euroregion founding documents, and practice examples by themes like mobility, institutional contact, and inclusion/exclusion.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: In legal project work, 'matrix' is a familiar term that sounds operationally specific, so both assume the other is picturing the standard format they personally use and neither sees a reason to define it.

misalignment_points.topic: Which cooperation programme file set is 'the CBC material'
misalignment_points.surface_form: They both refer to 'the CBC programme documents' and 'the current programme file.'
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Elena is thinking of the active 2021-2027 Interreg NEXT Romania-Ukraine programme documents that the steering group expects in the upcoming workshop packet.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Taras is thinking primarily of the 2014-2020 ENI CBC Romania-Ukraine programme set because that is the clearest legal-administrative record of the shift from older border logics to newer cooperative framing.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both file sets concern the same cross-border area and are often discussed in shorthand as the Romania-Ukraine CBC programme, so the label feels precise enough even though it silently points to different document collections.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree that the annexes and source pack should be 'ready to circulate' by Thursday.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Elena means ready for internal circulation to the steering group: clean headings, stable citations, and no major gaps, even if some translations and underlying quotations are still being checked.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Taras means ready for circulation only after quotation verification, bilingual title checking, and confirmation that cited institutional documents match the original-language versions.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both are using a normal project-status phrase that usually signals progress rather than a formal gate; because each assumes the other shares their professional standard for legal readiness, the phrase passes without challenge.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They speak about covering 'the frontier annex' and 'institutional contacts around the border.'
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Elena assumes the annex covers instruments and institutions directly tied to the Romania-Ukraine border area and the named bilateral/Euroregional arrangements discussed in the core memo.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Taras assumes the annex also includes adjacent frameworks that materially shape the frontier in practice, such as tri-border cooperation references and Black Sea regional documents that influence institutional contacts.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both agree on the broad narrative of cross-border cooperation, and the phrase 'around the border' sounds naturally inclusive without forcing either side to specify where the legal boundary of the annex actually stops.
